prompt: The 32 KiB, 8-way, 64-byte-line, 48-bit-physical-address L1 is write-back. Each line stores its tag, a valid bit and a dirty bit. Assume the same simple indexing model and ideal bit packing. Ignoring replacement, coherence, ECC/parity and array-layout overhead, how much extra storage does that metadata need?

options.explanation: Correct. 36 tag bits plus a valid and a dirty bit is 38 bits per line; 512 lines need 19,456 bits, which is 2,432 bytes, about 7.4% of 32,768 bytes.
A tag here is 36 bits, far more than one byte, so this badly undercounts.
This counts 38 bits for each of the 64 *sets*, but every line (every way) has its own tag, valid and dirty bits.
This uses 40 bits per line, i.e. a 38-bit tag. With 6 index and 6 offset bits removed from 48, the tag is 36.

workedExample:
1. Find the tag width:

```formula
S = C / (L E)
S = 32,768 B / (64 B × 8) = 64
s = log_2(64) = 6
b = log_2(64) = 6
t = m − s − b = 48 − 6 − 6 = 36
where
S: the number of sets
C: the data capacity, 32 KiB = 32,768 bytes
L: the line size, 64 bytes
E: ways per set, 8
s: index width, in bits
b: offset width, in bits
t: tag width, in bits
m: the physical address width, 48 bits
log_2: logarithm base 2: how many 2s you multiply together to reach the number; log_2(64) = 6
B: byte, 8 bits
KiB: kibibyte, 1,024 bytes
In words: with 6 index and 6 offset bits taken out of a 48-bit address, each tag is 36 bits.
```

2. Every line (every way of every set) stores its own tag, valid bit and dirty bit:

```formula
M_L = t + 1 + 1 = 38 bits
N = C / L = 32,768 / 64 = 512
M = N M_L
M = 512 × 38 = 19,456 bits
M = 19,456 / 8 = 2,432 B
f = 2,432 B / (32,768 B) ≈ 0.074
where
M_L: metadata bits per line: tag plus valid bit plus dirty bit
t: tag width, 36 bits
1: one valid bit, then one dirty bit
N: the number of lines, 512
C: the data capacity, 32,768 bytes
L: the line size, 64 bytes
M: total metadata for the whole cache
f: metadata as a fraction of the data capacity
8: bits per byte
≈: approximately equal to (rounded)
bits: binary digits, each 0 or 1
B: byte, 8 bits
In words: 38 bits for each of 512 lines is 2,432 bytes, about 7.4% on top of the 32 KiB of data.
```

A design may add replacement state (for example, 7 tree-PLRU bits per 8-way set), coherence bits and ECC/parity. Physical array layout also adds implementation-dependent overhead.
